result.title: GHC:Expanding Residual Interfaces in Hyper-Connections
result.summary: Hyper-Connections expand residual capacity across parallel streams, yet restrict every branch to narrow read and write interfaces: each branch still reads a single stream mixture and writes scaled copies of one output vector to all streams. To lift this bottleneck, we propose Grouped Hyper-Connections (GHC). By partitioning each branch into parallel groups along attention heads or FFN channels, GHC supplies each group with a distinct stream mixture and aggregates their separate outputs into each stream with learned weights. Extensive experiments across dense and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models show that GHC consistently improves upon Identity Hyper-Connections (IHC) with negligible parameter and memory-access overhead, increasing training efficiency by 35% over Pre-Norm and 10% over IHC. Moreover, expanding residual interfaces overcomes the diminishing returns of adding streams, allowing wider residual states to yield further gains.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Grouped Hyper-Connections（GHC），把每个分支按注意力头或 FFN 通道拆成并行组，让各组读取不同的残差流混合、并以学习权重把各自输出写回各流，在 dense 与 MoE 模型上以极小开销提升训练效率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「窄读／写接口限制并行残差流容量」的诊断与分组读写机制，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态宽度、多流状态更新与信息瓶颈设计提供可核查的架构借鉴，但不涉及视觉推理本身。
